rows.en:
Right.
You're someone who listens to advice, aren't you?
Yes, you have to listen to her advice.
You must not look back.
No matter what happens.
You told me so yourself, after all.
That you listen to advice.
Don't lie to me.
If you lie, I'll kill you.
I hate it.
I can't forgive liars.
Understood?
...You didn't look back.
Even so, the fear didn't go away.
With every step you took, the fear soaked deeper into every inch of you.{p}

And then the girl's hands, wrapped around your neck, began to feel as if they were squeezing.
Somehow, it was very hard to breathe.
With each jolt of your steps, her hands were without a doubt tightening around your neck.
Thin, cold, hard fingers were coiled firmly around your throat.
If you looked back, she might vanish.
If you shook her off, you might get away from her.{p}What will you do?
Turn around
Shake her off
Do nothing

My, how admirable of you.
If you turned around, you'd be ignoring her advice.
If you shook her off, you'd be breaking your promise to her.
You endured it desperately.
Yes, shielding a heart that felt ready to freeze solid with fear, you endured.{p}

"...What a long hallway, isn't it?
...I wonder when this hallway will ever end.
Was there ever a hallway this long at school...?"
Her voice, spoken to no one in particular, melted away into the darkness.
"...It's awfully cold, isn't it?"{p}

The moment she said that, a cold wind blew at you from behind.
And riding on the wind came a groaning voice, as if wrung from the pit of someone's belly.
A dank, hateful voice, like the dead of hell cursing and reviling the living from the depths of the earth.
It might have been the sound of the wind.
But then again, it might not have been the wind at all.
Her voice whispered at your ear again.
"...Scared, aren't ya?
Wanna try looking back?
Look back, and you can rest easy. You won't have to be scared anymore."{p}

A sweet, beckoning voice.
What will you do?
Will you look back?{p}If you don't look back, you might die.
Look back
Don't look back

"Eeeeeeeeeek!"
Suddenly an ear-splitting, high-pitched shriek rang out, and the thin fingers wrapped around your neck clenched tight.
"Stop it!"
That was all you could manage to scream.
...And then, you slipped away into unconsciousness.{p}

..........I'm sorry.
It wasn't you, was it?
It was the other {a}.
Yes, this was the story of the other you.
It was the next morning when he came to.
A student from his class helped him up.{p}

"What happened to you?
Why are you sleeping in a place like this?"
Even when asked that, he didn't know how to answer.
As his head cleared, he hurriedly looked up and down the hallway.{p}

The hallway was plainly visible in the morning light.
The usual hallway was there.
The usual hallway, where you could see from one end to the other.
And he had been lying in front of his classroom.
"...I made it."
That was all he could murmur.
Maybe it had been a dream.
Maybe he'd been worn out from studying and had a bad dream.
The classmate was giving him a strange look.
And then said:
"What's with you?
You've got a weird bruise on your neck."
At that, he checked in a mirror.{p}

On his neck were distinct finger marks, as if he had been strangled.
In the end, he never found out why the hallway had been so long.
Or what it was he had been carrying on his back.
If he had looked behind him, he might have learned what it really was.
Though he might have lost his life in exchange.{p}

The bruise on his neck didn't fade for about a month.
Even so, he survived.
Maybe it was thanks to keeping his promise to the very end.
You said you were in Class 1-E, didn't you?
If I remember right, that classroom is on the third floor.
Isn't Class 1-E that classroom at the end of the long hallway?{p}

But don't worry.
You're a kind person who keeps promises and listens to advice.
I'll pray that never changes.
Humans are creatures who change their minds so easily, after all.
...Heh heh heh heh, do be careful.
And that's the end of my story.
Now, who's speaking next?{p}

What a thing to say, out of nowhere.
Don't say such sad things.
Then I'm asking you, please.
Become a kind person from now on.
Otherwise, I can't talk with you.
I like kind people.
Now, give me your answer.{p}Are you a kind person?
I'm kind
I'm not kind

You're not confident in your own kindness?
It's all right.
I can tell.
You're a kind person.
Aren't you?
I want you to be able to say that you are.
I like kind people, you see.
Now, give me your answer.{p}Are you a kind person?
I'm kind
I'm not kind

I see...
So that's the kind of person you are.
Fine. Then promise me.
Promise that from now on, you'll be someone who keeps promises.
Please.
Now, I'll ask you once more.{p}Are you someone who can keep a promise?
I can keep my promises
I can't keep my promises

Don't put it like that.
Whenever you make a promise to someone, be the kind of person who always keeps it.
Please.
If you agree, give me your answer.
{a}...{p}You can keep a promise, can't you?
I can keep my promises
I can't keep my promises

Thank you.
You're a good person, aren't you?{p}
Then I'll ask you my last question.{p}

Heh heh...
Because this school is far too dangerous.
A tremendous spiritual aura swirls all through it.
Meeting you here, right now, must be some kind of fate.{p}

Listen, {a}.
Make sure you listen to other people's advice.
Otherwise...
I won't answer for whatever happens to you.
Now, give me your answer.{p}Do you listen to other people's advice?
I take people's advice to heart
I can't do that

I see...
That's one way to think, too.
But that won't get you anywhere at this school.
If you don't listen to all sorts of people's advice, you'll regret it later.
This school is far too dangerous.
A tremendous spiritual aura swirls all through it.
Meeting you here, right now, must be some kind of fate.
Listen, {a}.
Make sure you listen to other people's advice.
Otherwise...
I won't answer for whatever happens to you.
Now, give me your answer once more.{p}Do you listen to other people's advice?
I take people's advice to heart
I can't do that

I see...
What a shame.
I thought that if you were a kind person, you might be able to break the curse of the girl I'm about to tell you about...
This is the story of a pitiful girl.
I don't know how you'll feel about it, but that's how I see her.
This is the story of a pitiful girl.{p}

Long ago, there was a girl at this school named Natsumi Kitajima.
There was a boy she liked.
His name was... what was it, now?
I can't remember.
Let's see, suppose we call him {a}.
I'll borrow your name.
His name was {b} {a}.{p}

Kitajima just couldn't bring herself to confess.
She was in the same class as {a}, but day after day went by with her doing nothing but gazing at him from afar.{p}

And then, one hot summer day...
She was gazing at {a}, the way she always did.{p}

{a}'s face, {a}'s hair, {a}'s arms peeking out of his shirt...
She had extremely sharp eyes; they say she could even see the beads of sweat running down his arm.
And then a mosquito landed there.
He slapped the mosquito with his hand.
And a tiny smear of blood was left on {a}'s arm.
When she saw it, she felt a little strange.{p}

Outside the window, the cicadas were shrilling almost deafeningly.
A hot, hot summer day...
Looking at the mosquito that had sucked {a}'s blood, she found herself feeling somehow envious.
That mosquito could land on {a}'s arm and even drink his blood, and she envied it terribly.
She was so far away from him, and yet that mosquito.........{p}

Day after day, mosquito after mosquito landed on his arm.
It made her feel sick inside.
She couldn't even speak to {a}, and yet those mosquitoes...
She brooded over it until she even came to think that if she could drink {a}'s blood, she wouldn't mind being swatted dead like a mosquito.
Kitajima was terrified of herself for feeling that way.
So she decided to confess to {a}.
She gathered every ounce of courage and decided to tell him how she felt.{p}...How will you answer her?
Go out with her
Turn her down

The next day, the two of you decided to eat lunch together on the roof.
A boxed lunch, eaten together with her...
She looked so happy.
For a while, it was a fun time.
But...{p}

While you were eating your rolled omelet, she suddenly slapped your arm.
"I'm sorry.
There was a mosquito just now..."
That's what Kitajima said.{p}After that, she began slapping your arms and face at every chance she got.
Keep going out with her
Get away from her

And her behavior escalated more and more.
She simply could not forgive the mosquitoes for sucking your blood.
{a} is mine.
And yet the mosquitoes are still sucking {a}'s blood...
Whenever she thought about it, she couldn't stand still.
She couldn't forgive the mosquitoes that drank your blood, but she also grew unable to forgive you, for letting them drink it so easily.
And she became even more violent toward you than before.
When you scolded her for it, she burst into tears.{p}

After that, she couldn't stop thinking about your windpipe.
Every time you talked, she couldn't stop thinking about the way the flesh of your throat moved.
I might as well just...
She thought that, over and over again.
And then, one day...{p}

As you were eating lunch on the roof as usual, she suddenly sank her teeth into your windpipe...
It seems she was ready to die right then and there.
If she could drink your blood, she didn't care if she died.
That's how determined she was.
She bit into you with all her might.{p}

So hard that your throat could have torn right off...
.........
You fought back desperately and pinned her down.
Word of it spread around the school, and she transferred away.
And then...{p}

From then on, swarms of mosquitoes began breeding in the class she had been in.
And their target was... {a}, it was you.
No, it wasn't you, was it?
It was the {a} in this story.
The mosquitoes in that class didn't drink the blood of any other student.
They say they drank only {a}'s blood, every day, day after day.
They say that every day, day after day, they fed on his flesh all over his body...
A rumor went around the school that it was Kitajima's curse.
And they say that curse still hangs over that class today.{p}

That class was... Class 1-E.
Your class.
The curse, it seems, is that something speaks into the ear of a girl with an unrequited crush.
They say the voice says this:
"Make the one you love yours and yours alone.
To do that, you must drink their blood.
If you can't do it, I'll do it for you.
Well? Shall I send the mosquitoes under my command to drink their blood for you?"
And depending on how the girl answers, mosquitoes swarm through the class.{p}

...I feel sorry for Kitajima.
I'm sure she was led astray by whoever owns that voice.
I don't think the mosquito swarms were her curse.
I'm sure something in this school...
was what led her astray, I think.
{a}.
If a girl who fell for you heard that voice, what would you do?
I wonder if you could break the curse of that voice's owner...
That's the end of my story.
Whose turn is it next?{p}

Why would you have to turn her down?
She was so very sweet and modest.
So {a} was overjoyed to be confessed to.
And he decided to go out with her.
Listen.
You knew nothing of the terrible feelings that had taken root in her heart.{p}

You started to think there was something strange about the way she acted.
So one day, after some time had passed, you brought up breaking up with her.{p}

Then she burst into tears and clung to your chest.
She thought:
I'd finally gotten to be close enough to talk to him.
If I break up with {a}, the days of watching him from afar will start all over again.
I can't bear that...
As she was thinking that, her eyes fell on your throat.{p}

She remembered the mosquitoes that drank your blood, and an aching feeling came over her.
And then she did something even she could hardly believe.{p}

Yes, she sank her teeth into your windpipe.
She bit down with all her might.{p}

You'd say a thing like that?
That's a problem. There was something I wanted you to promise me...
I have a favor to ask of you, since you're so kind.
I want you to break the curse I'm about to tell you about.
...It may be an impossible thing to ask.
But I can't help telling you about it.
Because I feel so very sorry for the girl in this story.
...Listen carefully.{p}
